evidence:
What is right: all five prompts and app_context.md describe this app and carry no sibling-task residue. A grep of task/tests for sign in, login, password, account, credential, admin and other product names finds only app_context.md:8-10 ('## Accounts' / 'None. The app has no sign-in; every browser tab or context uses the same shared library.'), which agrees with instruction.md:5 and policy.md:3. The template's sign-in gate wording, forged-request rules and tenant-isolation rules were removed rather than left behind. Key screens (app_context.md:14) lists only controls the public notes require (ui.md:17, ui.md:9, ui.md:11). The health address (app_context.md:22) matches integration.md:3. The restart text (functional/prompt.md:31) names tool restart_app on server verifier, matching functional/judge.toml:15-18 and tools/restart_mcp.py:14, and exactly one criterion names it (functional/judge.toml:326). The three scored prompts restate one identical in-dimension gate (functional/prompt.md:5, polish/prompt.md:5, visual/prompt.md:5). The only placeholders are {app_context} and {criteria}; no CHANGE_ME remains. Canvas and static-picture notes (app_context.md:25-26) agree with ui.md:3 and behaviour.md:5.

Defect (inconsistency between prompt, context and criterion on script use for a replay): functional/prompt.md:20 says 'Do not dispatch synthetic events, do not change the app's DOM or state from script'. app_context.md:23 says clearing storage 'is the one permitted use of script to change browser state'. functional/prompt.md:22 then says 'Replaying a request you recorded from the app's own network activity is allowed where a criterion says so', and functional/judge.toml:353 (cw_history_restore_retry) requires 'Repeat the same already completed restore request through the control the app offers for retrying it, or by replaying the recorded request: no fifth revision may be created'. Playwright MCP has no replay tool, so the only way to replay is an in-page scripted request, which is a state-affecting script call that line 20 forbids and that app_context.md:23 excludes by naming storage clearing as the one permitted use. The template stated the mechanism ('Replays use an in-page call from the app's own origin carrying the app's session credential', template functional/prompt.md:41-42); the task prompt dropped that sentence and added nothing in its place. qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md requires ambiguous evidence to be defined consistently across prompt, context and criterion.

Notes, not counted as defects: (1) every prompt line 1 and app_context.md:3,6 call the product 'Colderwater', a name that appears nowhere in instruction.md, environment/instructions/*.md or seed_data.json (grep: only task.toml, tests and solution contain it), so a conforming submission will not be branded that way; the URL identifies the app and no criterion asks for the name, so impact is low, but 'Name: Colderwater playground' is not something the builder was told. (2) visual/prompt.md:7 states a 0 to 5 scale but omits the template's sentence (template visual/prompt.md:39-42) that the RewardKit-rendered '1 to 5' hint is boilerplate and the 0-5 anchors are authoritative; whether that hint is rendered was not measured here.

No configured judge run exists for this candidate, so the effect on a real judge session is not measured.
counterexample: Conforming alternative that can fail: an app that implements restore idempotency correctly but shows no visible 'retry restore' control (behaviour.md:13 requires only that a repeated request creates no extra revision, not a retry control). The judge must then replay the recorded request. Following functional/prompt.md:20 and app_context.md:23 literally it may not send a state-affecting request from script, so after two attempts it fails cw_history_restore_retry (weight 1.5) under functional/prompt.md:15, although the app is correct. Broken app that can pass: the same judge, unable to replay, treats the leg as satisfied because clicking the Restore control again produced a new, differently keyed request that the app legitimately handles, so a server that is not idempotent for a repeated identical request keeps the credit.
suggested_fix: In tests/scored/functional/prompt.md line 22, state the mechanism: a replay named by a criterion is made with one in-page request from the app's own origin that copies the recorded method, path, headers and body, and this is a permitted use of script. In tests/app_context.md line 23, change 'the one permitted use of script to change browser state' to say that clearing storage and a replay named by a criterion are the only permitted script uses. Optionally change 'Name: Colderwater playground' to say the name is the grader's label and the app need not display it, and restore the template sentence about the rendered 1-to-5 hint in the visual prompt.
